status: M0 draft: only cells verified against real LPSN names or the ICNP orthography appendix are populated as verified. Anything flagged verified:false is a documented PROPOSAL — the engine must never assert compliance from it.

rank_suffix_policy._note: The suffix table above separates mandatory ICNP terminations from terminations borrowed from the botanical code for intermediate ranks. The strength is explicit. The engine only asserts compliance for a suprageneric name whose stem is verified AND whose name is attested in data/type_genus_stems.json ('attested_higher_rank_names').

phylum.mandatory_under: SeqCode recommendation (phyla should end in -ota); ICNP 2022 list of suprageneric terminations

class.mandatory_under: SeqCode recommendation (classes should end in -ia); conserved historical class names are listed in conserved_names

order.mandatory_under: ICNP: order names are formed from the stem of the type-genus name + -ales
order.source: ICNP suprageneric rules; rule number not re-verified locally (rule_citation_status in type_genus_stems.json)

family.mandatory_under: ICNP: family names are formed from the stem of the type-genus name + -aceae
family.source: ICNP suprageneric rules; rule number not re-verified locally (rule_citation_status in type_genus_stems.json)

subclass.mandatory_under: not mandatory under ICNP; adopted from the botanical code for intermediate ranks

suborder.mandatory_under: not mandatory under ICNP; adopted from the botanical code for intermediate ranks

subfamily.mandatory_under: not mandatory under ICNP; adopted from the botanical code for intermediate ranks

tribe.mandatory_under: not mandatory under ICNP; adopted from the botanical code for intermediate ranks

subtribe.mandatory_under: not mandatory under ICNP; adopted from the botanical code for intermediate ranks

rank_suffix_example_type_genera._note: B1 machine check: scripts/verify_examples.py asserts generate(<type_genus>, 'feature', <rank>) reproduces every name in rank_suffix_examples. A name without a type genus here FAILS the check — typification is part of the rule, so a place name or an arbitrary string must never carry a -aceae suffix.

conserved_name_notes: Class 'Bacilli' and 'Gammaproteobacteria' are conserved historical class names that do not end in -ia; the engine must NOT flag them as errors.
Old phylum names such as 'Proteobacteria' are transitional retained names.
'Bacillia' is NOT a name: the class of Bacillus is the protected name 'Bacilli' (data/type_genus_stems.json higher_rank_exceptions). generate('Bacillus'|'Bacill', ..., 'class') must return 'Bacilli'.

conserved_names_detail._note: Conserved / protected / transitional suprageneric names the suffix rules must not be applied to. Only entries verified:true are treated as sourced; the rest await M0 sign-off against the ICNP lists (the code text itself is not in this repository).

Bacilli.source: ICNP list of protected names; LPSN lists Bacilli as the class of Bacillaceae

Clostridia.source: LPSN — stem 'clostridi' + -ia with vowel coalescence, NOT an exception

Omegaproteobacteria.source: name is in use; the rank/kind attribution was not re-verified locally

Proteobacteria.source: LPSN transitional name; replaced by Pseudomonadota

Firmicutes.source: LPSN transitional name; replaced by Bacillota

Cyanobacteria.source: LPSN transitional name; replaced by Cyanobacteriota

Bacteroidetes.source: LPSN transitional name; replaced by Bacteroidota

Chlamydiae.source: -ae style phylum name; kind/authority not re-verified locally

Thermotogae.source: -ae style phylum name; kind/authority not re-verified locally

epithet_adjective_notes.nourishing: Paradigm anchored to real LPSN names (Streptomyces autotrophicus m / Pseudonocardia autotrophica f). A bare '-trophus/-tropha/-trophum' paradigm, if sanctioned by the ICNP orthography appendix, is an M0 sign-off item — not guessable from memory.
epithet_adjective_notes.third_declension_removed_examples: 'Clostridium tertium' is not a noun-in-apposition example: -ium/-um is 2nd-declension neuter, and classifying it as one only appeared to pass because an unanalysable ending was mistaken for a noun in apposition.
epithet_adjective_notes.third_declension_caveat: Many -is epithets are common-gender (they do not switch to -e in the neuter), e.g. Mycobacterium tuberculosis — those are handled through epithet_indeclinable, never by forcing -e.
epithet_adjective_notes.origin_inus_note: -inus/-a/-um provenance adjectives are attested in classical toponymics, but no LPSN instance was inspected for this repository — M0 sign-off item.
epithet_adjective_notes.resembling_eus_note: -eus/-ea/-eion Greek 'resembling' adjectives: no prokaryotic instance inspected — M0 sign-off item.

place_adjective_formations._note: M2: a place epithet is not restricted to the -ensis/-ense family. validate_agreement() tries these formations in order and returns True for the first whose GENDER-FORM matches; a match on another gender's form is positive evidence of disagreement (False); no match at all is a needs-review, never a guessed False.
place_adjective_formations.source: anchors: Klebsiella michiganensis / Rhizobium mongolense (-ensis), Thermus aquaticus / Lactobacillus helveticus (-icus), Rhodopseudomonas palustris (3rd decl.)

epithet_indeclinable._note: M2: the 4th grammatical category — participle / common-gender adjective. Such epithets have ONE form for m, f and n, so gender agreement cannot fail and they must never be labelled 'noun in apposition'. storage/etymology.py renders them as 'N.L. part. adj.' / 'N.L. adj. common'.

endings.source: LPSN: Comamonas denitrificans, Bacillus… (-ans, present participle)
LPSN: Clostridium perfringens, Agrobacterium tumefaciens, Methylobacterium extorquens, Bacillus halodurans (-ans/-ens)

anchors.source: LPSN etymology 'N.L. adj. pyogenes' (Greek -ες, common gender)
LPSN; disease-name adjective that does not switch to -e before a neuter genus
LPSN gives 'N.L. gen. n. coli, of the colon' i.e. a GENITIVE noun, not a noun in apposition (needs expert sign-off; until then it is attested only as indeclinable)

inhabitant.source: compound in -cola ('inhabitant of …') is indeclinable in Latin apart from the vocative; no LPSN instance was inspected for this repository — M0 sign-off item
inhabitant.note: Consumed by engine/validate.py and engine/generate.py — an epithet ending in -cola is never declined for the genus gender, but because the rule is unverified the verdict is needs_review (compliant=None), never a silent ✓.

prohibited_patterns._note: B2: explicit ICNP prohibitions that the engine must gate on. Consumed by engine/validate.py::_prohibited_hits and engine/generate.py (self-referential epithet / already-inflected stem). 'verdict' says what validate must return: 'non_compliant' can never be True, 'needs_review' refuses to assert anything.

rules.source: ICNP Rule 20 note — the specific epithet may not repeat the name of the genus
ICNP Rule 20 note — nor may it be the latinized form of the genus name
orthographic defect: the supplied stem already carried the paradigm ending (stem 'tunicensis' + -ensis)
family/order/class/phylum names are formed from the stem of a TYPE GENUS name — a place or personal stem cannot carry -aceae (bench seed 'Beijingaceae')
control experiment: an arbitrary string ('qqqzz') must not be classified as a noun in apposition and stamped compliant

genus_formation_hints._note: Genus names have no mandatory suffix; these endings are optional, non-binding suggestions exposed by the CLI (--genus-suffix).
